name: Yaogan-1
notes: MILFirst Yaogan. SAR imaging, JB-5 class. 1 m res.

name: Yaogan-2
notes: MILOptical IMINT. JB-6 class, 0.8–1.5 m res.

name: Yaogan-3
notes: MILSAR imaging. JB-5 follow-on.

name: Yaogan-4
notes: MILOptical IMINT. JB-6 class.

name: Yaogan-5
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-6
notes: MILOptical IMINT. JB-6 class.

name: Yaogan-7
notes: MILOptical IMINT.

name: Yaogan-8
notes: MILJB-9 class. High-alt area surveillance / low-res mapping.

name: Yaogan-9 A/B/C
notes: MILELINT triplet cluster. JB-8 naval surveillance, NOSS-analogue.

name: Yaogan-10
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-11
notes: MILOptical IMINT. JB-6, 1.5 m res.

name: Yaogan-12
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-13
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-14
notes: MILOptical IMINT. Sub-meter capability.

name: Yaogan-15
notes: MILJB-9 class. High-alt area surveillance.

name: Yaogan-16 A/B/C
notes: MILELINT triplet. Naval SIGINT.

name: Yaogan-17
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-18
notes: MILOptical IMINT. Sub-meter.

name: Yaogan-19
notes: MILJB-9 class.

name: Yaogan-20 A/B/C
notes: MILELINT triplet.

name: Yaogan-21
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-22
notes: MILJB-9 high-alt area surveillance.

name: Yaogan-23
notes: MILOptical IMINT.

name: Yaogan-24
notes: MILOptical IMINT. Possible improved JB-6.

name: Yaogan-25 A/B/C
notes: MILELINT triplet. Anomalous perigee/apogee spread, highly elliptical loop.

name: Yaogan-26
notes: MILSAR imaging.

name: Yaogan-27
notes: MILJB-9 class. High-alt mapping.

name: Yaogan-28
notes: MILOptical IMINT.

name: Yaogan-29
notes: MILSAR imaging. JB-5 successor class, ~617 km.

name: Yaogan-30 Groups 01–10+
notes: MIL10+ triplet launches, 30+ sats. ELINT maritime surveillance. 35° inc. anomalous for SSO — naval focus. Each group 3 sats co-orbital.

name: Yaogan-31 A/B/C
notes: MILELINT triplet. 50° inclination, global coverage focus.

name: Yaogan-32 01 A/B
notes: DUALDual-satellite optical pair. LM-2D from Jiuquan.

name: Yaogan-33
notes: MILLaunch failure. LM-4C upper stage malfunction. Replacement: Yaogan-33R.

name: Yaogan-33R
notes: MILSAR imaging. Replacement for Yaogan-33. Higher orbit than predecessor.

name: Yaogan-34
notes: DUALOptical remote sensing. Official: Belt and Road support, land surveying.

name: Yaogan-34-02
notes: DUALOptical remote sensing.

name: Yaogan-34-03
notes: DUALOptical remote sensing.

name: Yaogan-34-04
notes: DUALOptical remote sensing.

name: Yaogan-35 Groups 01–04
notes: MIL4 groups, multiple sats per group. LM-2D. Likely optical cluster.

name: Yaogan-36 Groups 01–04
notes: MILELINT triplets. 35° inclination. Follow-on to Yaogan-30 series.

name: Yaogan-37 Groups 01–03
notes: MILOptical imaging. LM-4B launches.

name: Yaogan-38
notes: MILReconnaissance. LM-2D Jiuquan.

name: Yaogan-39 Groups 01–03
notes: MILTriplet ELINT clusters. 50° inclination.

name: Yaogan-40 Groups 01–02
notes: MIL3 sats/group. Electromagnetic environment detection. LM-6A Taiyuan.

name: Yaogan-41
notes: MILCLASSGEO persistent wide-area optical surveillance. Successor to Gaofen-13. CSIS: principal GEO ISR platform.

name: Yaogan-42
notes: MILOptical. LM-4B.

name: Yaogan-43 Groups 01–03
notes: MIL18+ sats in 3 batches. 'New technology test for low-orbit constellations.' Likely ISR/ELINT constellation precursor.

name: Yaogan-44
notes: MILOptical. LM-2D.

name: Yaogan-45
notes: MILCLASSAnomalous 7,500 km MEO. Wide-field ISR / possible SIGINT. Passes through Van Allen belt. LM-7A Wenchang.

name: Yaogan-46
notes: MILSecond MEO ISR. LM-7A. Companion to YG-45.

name: Yaogan-47
notes: MILImagery satellite. LM-4B Jiuquan. Latest in series.

name: Gaofen-1
notes: DUAL0.8 m PAN, 3.2 m MS. Revisit ≤4 days. CAST2000 bus. Civil primary user.

name: Gaofen-2
notes: DUAL0.81 m PAN, 3.24 m MS. China's first sub-meter civil satellite.

name: Gaofen-3
notes: DUAL1–500 m resolution SAR, 12 imaging modes. All-weather day/night. 2,279 kg.

name: Gaofen-3 02
notes: DUALFollow-on SAR to GF-3. Expanded imaging modes.

name: Gaofen-4
notes: DUAL50 m EOIS optical. First GEO optical remote sensing satellite. 3 images/min. At 105.6°E.

name: Gaofen-5
notes: DUAL6 instruments: hyperspectral, atmospheric. First Chinese high-res atmospheric pollution satellite.

name: Gaofen-5 02
notes: DUALImproved hyperspectral instruments.

name: Gaofen-6
notes: DUAL2 m PAN + 8 m MS + 16 m wide-field. Agronomic monitoring.

name: Gaofen-7
notes: DUAL0.8 m sub-meter stereo. Topographic mapping. First Chinese stereo sub-meter sat.

name: Gaofen-8
notes: MILLikely Yaogan-lineage. 0.5 m res suspected. From Taiyuan.

name: Gaofen-9 series (01–06)
notes: DUALAgile 0.5 m PAN, 3-DoF attitude freedom. Rapid tasking.

name: Gaofen-10
notes: DUALPreviously failed launch in 2016 (GF-10A lost). Replacement success 2019.

name: Gaofen-11 01/02/03
notes: DUALSub-0.5 m resolution. Highest resolution civil Chinese satellites. Some orbit 250 km — very low for maintenance cost.

name: Gaofen-12 01/02/03
notes: DUALSAR constellation. Meter-level resolution. Multiple imaging modes.

name: Gaofen-13
notes: DUAL~15 m res est. GEO optical. At ~100°E. Believed Changchun optics.

name: Gaofen-13 02
notes: DUAL~15 m res est. GEO optical. Second in series.

name: Gaofen-14 01
notes: DUAL0.5 m stereo surveying. DEM generation.

name: Gaofen-14 02
notes: DUALSecond stereo surveying satellite. LM-3B Xichang.

name: Ludi Tance-4
notes: DUALWorld's FIRST GEO SAR satellite. 20 m resolution. Cloud-penetrating, day/night. Officially: land resources and disaster. LM-3B Xichang.

name: Tianhui-1-01
notes: DUALStereo cartographic mapping. 5 m resolution.

name: Tianhui-1-02
notes: DUALMapping. Follow-on.

name: Tianhui-1-03
notes: DUALMapping continuation.

name: Tianhui-2-01/02
notes: DUALDual-satellite stereo mapping pair. Improved resolution.

name: Tianhui-7
notes: DUALLatest stereo cartographic satellite. LM-4B.

name: BeiDou-1A/B/C (BDS-1)
notes: Experimental regional RDSS+RNSS. Two-way ranging. 3 GEO sats. BDS-1 epoch.

name: COMPASS-M1
notes: First BDS MEO test satellite. Validated signal design for BDS-2/3.

name: BeiDou-2 IGSO 1–7
notes: 7 IGSO sats at 55° inclination. Regional augmentation. BDS-2 service.

name: BeiDou-2 MEO 1–7
notes: 7 MEO sats. BDS-2 global navigation component. B1I/B2I/B3I signals.

name: BeiDou-2 GEO 1–6
notes: 5 active GEO. SBAS service over Asia-Pacific. RDSS messaging.

name: BeiDou-3 IGSO-1 (C38)
notes: BDS-3 IGSO first satellite. New B1C/B2a signals.

name: BeiDou-3 IGSO-2 (C39)
notes: BDS-3 IGSO second.

name: BeiDou-3 IGSO-3 (C40)
notes: BDS-3 IGSO third. Completes IGSO plane.

name: BeiDou-3 GEO-1 (C59)
notes: BDS-3 first GEO. B1C/B3I. SBAS corrections.

name: BeiDou-3 GEO-2 (C60)
notes: BDS-3 GEO second.

name: BeiDou-3 GEO-3 (C61)
notes: Final BDS-3 satellite. Constellation declared complete 23 Jun 2020. B1C/B2a/B3I.

name: BeiDou-3 MEO Block 1 (C19–C30)
notes: 10 MEO sats in 2018 alone. Walker 24/3/1 constellation. ~21,500 km. B1C/B2a/B3I/B2b signals.

name: BeiDou-3 MEO Block 2 (C31–C37, C45–C50)
notes: Remaining 17 MEO sats completing Walker 24+3 spare configuration. Global service.

name: BeiDou-3 augmentation (C43, new batch 2023)
notes: New augmentation/replacement batch. Enhanced signals, longer design life. 20 new sats planned.

name: Tianlian-1-01
notes: First Chinese data relay satellite. DFH-3 bus. LM-3C maiden flight. 15%→70% LEO coverage.

name: Tianlian-1-02
notes: DFH-3 bus. Extends relay coverage.

name: Tianlian-1-03
notes: DFH-3 bus. 70%+ orbital coverage achieved.

name: Tianlian-1-04
notes: DFH-3 bus. Enhanced bandwidth. Crewed spaceflight relay.

name: Tianlian-1-05
notes: Final Gen I. DFH-3 bus.

name: Tianlian-2-01
notes: DFH-4 bus. Higher bandwidth. Tiangong CSS primary relay.

name: Tianlian-2-02
notes: DFH-4 bus. Near-100% LEO relay coverage.

name: Tianlian-2-03
notes: DFH-4 bus. Supports Tiangong CSS and future missions.

name: Tianlian-2-04
notes: DFH-4 bus. 4th Gen II relay sat.

name: Tianlian-2-05
notes: DFH-4 bus. Completes Gen II constellation.

name: ChinaSat-5A (Apstar-9A)
notes: DFH-3. C/Ku-band. 142°E. Leased to APT Satellite.

name: ChinaSat-6B
notes: DFH-4. C/Ku-band. 115.5°E. Television/broadband.

name: ChinaSat-6D
notes: DFH-4E. 125°E. DTH television for mainland China.

name: ChinaSat-9B
notes: DFH-4E. 92.2°E. DTH direct-to-home TV broadcast.

name: ChinaSat-16 (Shijian-13)
notes: DFH-4E. 110.5°E. First Chinese Ka-band HTS. 50 Gbps throughput. Electric propulsion.

name: ChinaSat-1A (Feng Huo-2-1)
notes: MILDFH-4. Military Ku-band comms. PLA ground forces secure links.

name: ChinaSat-1B
notes: MILDFH-4. Military comms. PLA network.

name: ChinaSat-1C
notes: MILDFH-4E. Enhanced military comms.

name: ChinaSat-10
notes: DFH-4. 103.5°E. Broadband and broadcasting. Replaced by ChinaSat-10R.

name: ChinaSat-10R
notes: DFH-4E. 103.5°E. Replaces ChinaSat-10. LM-3B/E Xichang.

name: ChinaSat-9C
notes: DFH-4E. DTH domestic broadcast replacement satellite. LM-3B Xichang.

name: Zhongxing-4A
notes: MILLM-7A Wenchang. First of new believed military comms class. Dual-use capacity assessed.

name: Shijian-20
notes: Maiden DFH-5 bus flight. ~8,000 kg. High-throughput comms + tech demo. Electric propulsion.

name: FY-1A
notes: Experimental. 39 days operational; attitude control failure.

name: FY-1B
notes: Experimental. ~2 years; attitude control failure again.

name: FY-1C
notes: Operational. Destroyed by Chinese ASAT 11 Jan 2007. Created 3,000+ debris objects. WMO designated.

name: FY-1D
notes: Operational. 10-year mission life. Final FY-1 series.

name: FY-2A
notes: Spin-stabilized. S-VISSR imager. DFH-2A bus. 86.5°E graveyard.

name: FY-2B
notes: 2nd GEO weather sat. SAST-built.

name: FY-2C
notes: Operational GEO. 105°E.

name: FY-2D
notes: GEO operational. DCS capability. 86.5°E.

name: FY-2E
notes: 105°E. Improved S-VISSR.

name: FY-2F
notes: 112.5°E. Final operational FY-2 for western coverage.

name: FY-2G
notes: 86.5°E then 105°E. Near-real-time Typhoon monitoring.

name: FY-2H
notes: 79°E (Indian Ocean focus). Covers South Asia, IOC.

name: FY-3A
notes: Second-gen polar. 10+ instruments. Morning orbit.

name: FY-3B
notes: Afternoon orbit. Complements FY-3A.

name: FY-3C
notes: Operational. GNOS radio occultation added.

name: FY-3D
notes: Afternoon orbit. First aurora imager (WAAI). Space environment monitoring.

name: FY-3E
notes: World's FIRST early-morning orbit weather satellite. Fills 6-hour observation gap. WindRAD sea wind radar.

name: FY-3F
notes: Morning orbit. Enhanced HIRAS sounder. GAS greenhouse gas sensor.

name: FY-3G
notes: Precipitation radar focus (Ku/Ka-band). Low 407 km altitude, 50° inc for tropical coverage. First Chinese precipitation-measuring satellite.

name: FY-4A
notes: 3-axis stabilized. AGRI 16-band (500 m vis), GIIRS sounder, GLI lightning mapper. 104.7°E. WMO primary.

name: FY-4B
notes: Improved FY-4A. 250 m fast imager. 123.5°E. New water vapor channels.

name: Shijian-1
notes: China's 2nd satellite. Magnetometer + cosmic ray detector. Historical milestone.

name: Shijian-4
notes: Space environment monitoring. Radiation belt study.

name: Shijian-5
notes: With FY-1C. Space environment, particle radiation.

name: Shijian-6 A/B
notes: Space environment monitoring pair. SJ-6-01 through 04 followed in 2006-2010.

name: Shijian-9 A/B
notes: Tech demo pair. Space debris observation, new propulsion tests.

name: Shijian-12
notes: MILFirst Chinese co-orbital rendezvous (2010). Maneuvered alongside SJ-6F. RPO precursor.

name: Shijian-15
notes: MILTech demo. Space environment + maneuverability.

name: Shijian-17
notes: MILFirst Chinese GEO robotic arm. Positioned within 55 km of other GEO sats. Ranged 37.7°E–180°E. USSPACECOM flagged 2021 for counter-space risk.

name: Shijian-18
notes: LM-5 failure 45 min post-launch. DFH-5 maiden bus; 7,600 kg — would have been heaviest GEO sat. Lost in Pacific.

name: Shijian-19
notes: Recoverable science satellite. 12-day mission. Returned to Earth with biological/materials experiments.

name: Shijian-20
notes: DFH-5 bus demo. ~8,000 kg. Ka/Q/V-band comms tech tests + electric propulsion.

name: Shijian-21
notes: MILJan 2022: docked with defunct BeiDou G2 via robotic arm; moved G2 to 36,000 km graveyard orbit. First satellite relocation. Refueled by SJ-25 in 2025.

name: Shijian-22 A/B
notes: Tech demo pair. Space environment and formation flying.

name: Shijian-23
notes: High-inclination orbit. Space environment in radiation belt region.

name: Shijian-24 A/B
notes: Dual tech demo sats. New propulsion and SSA sensor tests.

name: Shijian-25
notes: MILOn-orbit refueling mission. Demonstrated propellant transfer with SJ-21. Mission extension service precursor.

name: Shijian-26
notes: GEO communications and tech demo. LM-3B.

name: Shijian-27 (6 sats)
notes: 6-satellite cluster. Space environment monitoring + SSA. LM-2C.

name: Shijian-28
notes: CLASSSettled at 116.9°E, 5° inclination. No details released. Monitored by open-source analysts. LM-7A Wenchang.

name: Shijian-29 A/B
notes: MILDual GEO sats. 'Space target detection' verification. SSA/inspection capability. ~3,500 kg each. LM-7A Wenchang.

name: Shijian-30 A/B/C
notes: Triplet. Space environment exploration + tech verification. 52° inclination. LM-2C Jiuquan.

name: TJS-1
notes: MILCLASSSIGINT. ~32 m unfurlable Ka-band dish suspected. 154.5°E. CAST-built.

name: TJS-2
notes: MILCLASSMissile early warning (Huoyan-1). SAST/DFH-4 derived. IR detector. 66.5°E. TJS-22 may be replacement.

name: TJS-3
notes: MILCLASSPlus sub-satellite. Sub-sat performed synchronized maneuvers Jan 2019 — GEO belt inspection. Unique unknown mission class.

name: TJS-4
notes: MILCLASSSIGINT. Ka-band dish. Follow-on to TJS-1.

name: TJS-5
notes: MILCLASSMissile early warning. SAST. Over South China Sea.

name: TJS-6
notes: MILCLASSMissile early warning. Over Oceania.

name: TJS-7
notes: MILCLASSEarly warning / SIGINT. LM-3B.

name: TJS-9
notes: MILCLASSSIGINT. Over Micronesia. 3rd Qianshao-3 class.

name: TJS-10
notes: MILCLASSMissile early warning. Year end LM-3B.

name: TJS-11
notes: MILCLASSLikely SIGINT. Similar to TJS-20, TJS-23 class. LM-3B.

name: TJS-12
notes: MILCLASSMissile EW. 8th TJS in ~18 months.

name: TJS-13
notes: MILCLASSFirst TJS in Molniya-like orbit. Persistent polar ICBM warning coverage. Follows Shiyan-10 experiments. LM-3C.

name: TJS-14
notes: MILCLASSEarly warning. 1st 2025 TJS. LM-7A Wenchang.

name: TJS-15
notes: MILCLASS90.2°E. LM-7A. Mission patch: King of the South (Four Heavenly Kings motif).

name: TJS-16
notes: MILCLASS152.5°E. LM-3B. Co-located near TJS-17.

name: TJS-17
notes: MILCLASS152.8°E. Above Papua New Guinea. ~200 km from TJS-16.

name: TJS-19
notes: MILCLASSSAST-built. LM-3C Xichang. Comms/SIGINT GEO. 9th TJS of 2025.

name: TJS-20
notes: MILCLASSPossible SIGINT. Same class as TJS-11, TJS-23.

name: TJS-21
notes: MILCLASSMolniya orbit. 51° inclination. Persistent northern coverage early warning. Likely operational follow-on to Shiyan-10 pair. LM-3B Xichang.

name: TJS-22
notes: MILCLASS66.5°E — co-located with TJS-2. Possible TJS-2 replacement/augmentation. LM-7A.

name: TJS-23
notes: MILCLASSLM-5 Wenchang. Heaviest in TJS series. SIGINT class. 9th TJS launch in 2025.

name: DAMPE / Wukong
notes: Dark matter indirect detection. Cosmic-ray measurement 5 GeV–100 TeV. 3× design life. CAS NSSC.

name: QUESS / Micius
notes: Quantum key distribution (1,200 km). Quantum entanglement + teleportation. First satellite QKD in history.

name: HXMT / Insight
notes: Hard X-ray astronomy. 1–250 keV. Observed neutron star mergers, pulsar timing. First Chinese X-ray telescope.

name: Taiji-1
notes: Gravitational wave precursor. Laser interferometry at pm precision. Technology validation for future Taiji constellation.

name: GECAM A/B
notes: Gravitational wave electromagnetic counterpart monitor. All-sky gamma-ray survey.

name: GECAM-C / SATech-01
notes: Enhanced gamma-ray monitor. Launched with SATech commercial demo.

name: ASO-S / Kuafu-1
notes: Solar flare + CME + magnetism. Full-disk solar observation. FMG magnetograph + Lyα imager + SUTRI corona imager.

name: Einstein Probe
notes: Wide-field X-ray transient monitor. Lobster-eye optics. 3,600 deg² FoV. China-ESA-MPE joint mission.

name: SMILE
notes: Solar-wind magnetosphere interaction. Highly elliptical 'SMILE orbit'. X-ray imager + plasma analyzer. China-ESA joint.

name: Double Star TC-1/TC-2
notes: First ESA-China joint mission. Magnetosphere and particle studies. Operated in concert with Cluster.

name: Tanpopo/Chang'e 5T1 DRO
notes: Lunar return capsule test. Circumlunar flight, biological experiments in space, successful recovery.

name: Haiyang-1A
notes: Ocean color/temperature. 1st Chinese ocean sat. 10-band COCTS + CZI imager.

name: Haiyang-1B
notes: Ocean color/temperature. 2nd generation. COCTS + CZI.

name: Haiyang-1C
notes: 3rd gen. Paired with HY-1D. COCTS, CZI, coastal zone imager. Doubled coverage.

name: Haiyang-1D
notes: Paired with HY-1C for daily global ocean color coverage. SOA-operated.

name: Haiyang-2A
notes: Ocean dynamics. Microwave scatterometer (sea wind), radar altimeter, MWRI. 1,575 kg.

name: Haiyang-2B
notes: Sea wind + wave + SST microwave. Operational HY-2 series begins.

name: Haiyang-2C
notes: 66° inclination (not SSO). Forms 3-sat ocean dynamics constellation with HY-2B/D. All-time coverage.

name: Haiyang-2D
notes: Completes HY-2 3-satellite constellation. 4-hour revisit on any ocean point.

name: Haiyang-4-01
notes: First high-precision global ocean salinity satellite. Comprehensive aperture radiometer. Novel active+passive detectors.

name: Ziyuan-1-02D (ZY-1-02D)
notes: Hyperspectral (166 bands) + visible. Land resources, mineral mapping.

name: Ziyuan-1-02E (ZY-1-02E)
notes: Enhanced hyperspectral + multispectral. Land survey.

name: Ziyuan-3-01 (ZY-3-01)
notes: First Chinese operational stereo mapping satellite. 2.5 m nadir. DEM generation.

name: Ziyuan-3-02 (ZY-3-02)
notes: Follow-on stereo. Enhanced cameras. Revisit improvement.

name: Huanjing-1A/B
notes: Dual-satellite environmental + disaster monitoring. 30 m optical + SAR (HJ-1B). Small-sat cluster concept.

name: Huanjing-2A/B
notes: 2nd gen. 16 m MS + 48 m hyperspectral + IR. Dual-satellite constellation.

name: Qianfan / G60 — Test batch (6 sats)
notes: First Qianfan launch. 6 test satellites. 1,160 km orbit. Ku/Q/V-band.

name: Qianfan Polar Group 01–04 (18×4 sats)
notes: 72 sats (4 groups × 18). Polar orbit shell. Operated by Shanghai Spacesail.

name: Qianfan Polar Groups 05–06+ (18× sats)
notes: Ongoing deployment. ~90 total in orbit end-2025 vs 648 Phase-1 target.

name: Guowang Group 01–03+ (10+ sats/launch)
notes: 100+ sats by Nov 2025. Two orbit shells. Dual-use ISR payload reported. Operated by China Satnet.

name: Tianqi-01 to -36
notes: 36 narrow-band IoT satellites. Asset tracking + messaging. Guodian Gaoke.

name: Geespace / Geely constellation (20+ sats)
notes: Commercial IoT + imagery + direct-to-device. Geely Auto-backed. 6,000 planned.
